A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same parallel ANN-SNN conversion work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original conversion-accuracy experiments in Tables 3–4 and inference-speed measurements in Figures 2 and S1.

after.justification: V2 retains the original conversion-accuracy experiments and inference-speed measurements, including the appendix analysis.

M1.justification: The parallel conversion matrices, DA-QCFS calibration, ReLU conversion stages, and inference optimizations are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retitled, but its procedural content is identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-1k classification, retaining the same conventional and training-free conversion scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluation domain is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 3–4 and the parallel-versus-serial inference comparisons. The newly cited FTBC work is discussed in related work but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The architectures, simulation and inference horizons, accuracy metrics, calibration procedure, and speed-measurement settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the one-epoch calibration and 1,000-image subset for timing IF neurons.

E4.justification: The calibration comparisons, inference-speed analysis, and Appendix A.3 speed-versus-accuracy analysis are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 4's parenthesized values remain accuracy differences from the ANN, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 3–4 match, including 72.90% for calibrated ImageNet-1k ResNet-34 at four steps. Figures 2 and S1 retain the same plotted results and reported speed trends.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 refines the expectation argument's assumption by specifying uniform input-current distributions within multiple subintervals and identifying the QCFS-to-QCFS step that requires it. V1 described uniform distributions more generally in Section 4.2. The theorem statement, equations, and derivation otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about lossless parallel conversion, calibration, computational efficiency, and low-latency performance.

C2.justification: V1 already distinguishes distribution-independent exact conversion from distribution-dependent equality in expectation in Section 4.2. V2 clarifies that distinction in the proof without changing the substantive interpretation. Experimental interpretations remain unchanged, and the new Impact Statement supplies no specific limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access URL to the abstract, absent from v1. The existing optimizer, hyperparameters, calibration instructions, hardware, and inference-optimization disclosures are retained; the linked resource itself was not inspected.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Wu et al. (2024), FTBC, as prior work on forward temporal bias correction, with a corresponding bibliography entry. The broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 updates the author and affiliation information, adds Acknowledgments and an Impact Statement, retitles Algorithm 1, and adds brief explanatory text. The main narrative and section organization are substantially retained.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint is extensively reformatted into a two-column ICML main text with running headers. Tables and figures are enlarged and repositioned, and Algorithm 1 fits in one column instead of spanning pages. The appendices remain single-column; display contents are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves code-access documentation, makes the distributional condition behind Appendix A.1 more precise, and adds relevant FTBC context. These provide limited gains in reproducibility information and clarity while preserving the method and empirical evidence. The extensive layout revision does not constitute a comparable scientific advance.
